messages.subject: spatial field varies across years
parts:
Dear all,

I built a model assuming that the spatial field is constant over year:
form.1 <-  y ~ 0 + b0 +  f(year, model="iid") + f(s, model=spde)

The effect of year and spatial field are shown in the following plots:






























In comparison, I built another model to allow the spatial field to vary across years:
form.2 <-  y ~ 0 + b0 +  f(year, model="iid") + f(s, model=spde, replicate=s.repl) 

The effect of year and spatial field are 

It seems like that in the second model, the year effect was included in the spatial field, so the year effect was nearly zero and the spatial effect was negative.Is there any way to allow me to maintain the year effect in the first plot and still get changing spatial field across years?
Thank you!Ruby

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spatial field varies across years
parts:
Hi,
yes, your spatio-temporal model is confounded with the year effect. You can impose
a simple integrate-to-zero constraint on the spatial fields, via
  spde <- inla.spde2.(pc)matern(..., constr=TRUE)

Also note that if you have an intercept in the model (b0 in your formula I presume) then
your year effect will _also_ be confounded with the intercept; rw2 models have a default sum-to-zero constraint, but not iid models.
In my attached test case, I left out b0 instead of imposing additional constraints on the year effect.

Empirical, unconstrained, and spde-constrained estimates below. See attached file for full example.

Finn

about constraints for replicate models; the constraints are also
replicated. the same is the case with group.

from what I read out of the discussion, the results seems ok in the

sum to zero, then I'll guess you'll get something inbetween these two
results.
